purpose: Rules for generating and labeling synthetic MuJoCo frames for the search network and the R15 pad finder, plus radio-first policy evaluation.

conventions.severity: hard means the scene, frame, or label must be rejected, masked, or relabeled; soft means a required dataset property or composition target.
conventions.parameter_rule: Numeric defaults are starting points. Calibrate them from projected pixel size, camera intrinsics, and held-out validation; they are not universal physical constants.

rules.title: Keep the drone body above the boat and the camera above the deck
rules.condition: At spawn and for every recorded approach frame, the drone's lowest physical point is not strictly above the target boat's highest point, excluding only the thin camera rod from the boat-height measurement; or the camera is below the deck plane.
rules.label_instruction: Do not emit frames or labels for the scene.
rules.rationale: Below-deck and collision-invalid views are not representative of the intended approach and can teach pad or boat appearance from impossible angles.

rules.title: Do not require identity when the target and similar boats are not visually distinguishable
rules.condition: The only difference between the target boat and a similar boat is hidden metadata, a map or scene seed, or a visual signature that is not resolvable at the rendered range and angle.
rules.label_instruction: Do not force target_boat or different_boat. Keep detection labels if the boats are visible, but remove identity supervision and use target_or_similar or unknown_boat for the ambiguous case.
rules.rationale: An identity label that cannot be inferred from the image teaches noise and makes the model appear wrong when the task is actually impossible.

rules.title: Only label what is actually visible and resolvable in the rendered frame
rules.condition: The boat or pad is outside the image, fully occluded, below the minimum projected size, or below the minimum contrast or sharpness threshold.
rules.label_instruction: Mask the affected heat, offset, evidence, identity, presence, or pad-center label, or mark the region as ignore. Do not treat missing visibility as a negative or background label.
rules.rationale: The absence of a label must mean the object is not there, not that the camera was pointed badly or the object was too small to see.
prevents: false negatives caused by bad framing

rules.title: Exclude search frames where the target boat overwhelms the frame
rules.condition: The projected target boat covers more than the maximum allowed fraction of the image, or there is too little surrounding context to learn search behavior. Camera distance alone is not a rejection: a close view that still shows enough of the hull and its centre is usable.
rules.label_instruction: Exclude the frame from search-network training. Mask the visible hull so it is not taught as background; do not reuse the frame as a negative example.
rules.rationale: The search network is trained for acquisition in a wider scene, not for close-up texture recognition. Extreme close-ups teach the wrong scale and remove the context needed to distinguish a boat from background.
prevents: search behavior learned from non-search views

rules.title: Require enough of the target boat to be visible for search
rules.condition: Less than 40 percent of the target boat's projected visible mask is inside the image, or truncation makes the boat center or extent ambiguous.
rules.label_instruction: Exclude the frame from search training. If it is kept for robustness analysis, mask the boat label rather than teaching a partial center.
rules.rationale: A boat that is mostly outside the frame cannot support a reliable center, scale, or identity label, and the missing part creates an unlearnable target.

parameters.calibration_note: Raised from 0.25 after the 6.6 m half-visible case measured 57% bbox visible with the true centre in frame.

rules.title: Reject search frames where the boat is too small or degraded to detect
rules.condition: A boat's projected extent is below the minimum detectable size, or the boat is present but contrast, blur, or resolution makes it unreliable to detect.
rules.label_instruction: Do not label empty sea when a boat is present but unresolvable. Exclude the frame from detection training or mark the boat region as unknown or ignore.
rules.rationale: Distance alone does not decide whether a boat is learnable; projected size and image quality do. Labeling an unresolvable boat as absent creates false negatives.

rules.title: Use ambiguous identity labels when the target signature is not resolvable
rules.condition: The target or similar boat is detectable, but the visible feature that distinguishes target_boat from different_boat is below the resolvable pixel, contrast, or occlusion limit.
rules.label_instruction: Keep heat, offset, and evidence labels if the boat is visible. Do not set identity to target or different, and do not count the frame as a target-confirmation example. Use target_or_similar or unknown_boat.
rules.rationale: Detection and identity have different resolution requirements. A boat can be easy to see while its identity cue is impossible to read, and forcing the identity label creates contradictory supervision.

rules.title: Handle overlapping boats without inventing a clean label
rules.condition: Two boats' projected centers land in the same heat cell, or their visible masks overlap enough that their centers or identities are ambiguous.
rules.label_instruction: Do not choose target versus decoy using hidden simulator identity. Mark the affected cells or regions ignore, or label both as unknown until they are visually separable.
rules.rationale: A heat cell can hold only one positive. Choosing a winner from privileged truth teaches the network to guess and makes tracker identity unstable.

rules.title: Require matched hard negatives and remove shortcut correlations
rules.condition: The dataset lacks similar-but-different boats, or target labels correlate with map, background, weather, time, boat color, or scene position.
rules.label_instruction: Add matched target and similar-boat pairs that differ only by a visible signature. Randomize nuisance factors and keep target labels independent of scene identity. If the only difference is hidden, apply R002.
rules.rationale: The search network must learn the boat and its visible identity cue, not the map or the weather. Matched hard negatives expose the real decision boundary.

rules.title: Do not turn unresolvable degradation into a negative example
rules.condition: Blur, glare, underexposure, rain, spray, compression, or horizon washout makes a boat or pad present but unresolvable.
rules.label_instruction: If the object cannot be resolved, mask its labels or exclude the frame. Include mild realistic degradation separately with clean labels; do not label degraded-but-present objects as absent.
rules.rationale: Robustness comes from learning to detect under realistic degradation, not from calling invisible objects background.
prevents: label noise under glare or blur

rules.title: Evaluate search lock on sequences, not independent frames
rules.condition: The dataset or evaluation contains only independent frames, or target lock, confirmation, and handoff are judged from a single image.
rules.label_instruction: Generate sequences covering approach, range change, camera motion, occlusion, reacquisition, and multiple boats. Keep per-frame labels, but judge lock and confirmation over time.
rules.rationale: The search network is per-frame, but permission to approach or land depends on track stability and state-machine confirmation.

rules.title: Keep pad-finder views within the resolvable range and avoid overfilled pad frames
rules.condition: The frame is beyond the maximum pad-finder range, or the pad overfills the frame so its center is not visible. Close-range views are allowed while the pad pattern and center remain visible.
rules.label_instruction: Exclude from pad-finder training when the pad is too far or an unusable close-up. Do not use distant boat-scale views as pad negatives, and do not use overfilled close-ups where the center is outside the image.
rules.rationale: The pad finder is not a boat detector. It should learn the pad pattern at acquisition and landing ranges. A close view with a visible, well-framed pad is a valid landing sample, not a reject; only overfilled or unresolvable close-ups are excluded.
prevents: center labels from outside the frame

rules.title: Label the pad center only when the pad pattern is resolvable
rules.condition: The pad center or enough of the pad pattern is outside the image, occluded, below the minimum projected size, or below the contrast or sharpness threshold.
rules.label_instruction: Do not emit a center or offset label from an unresolvable pad. Presence may stay true only if the pad is visibly present; otherwise exclude the frame.
rules.rationale: A pad center is a geometric label. If the geometry is not visible, the network cannot learn it and will memorize noise.

rules.title: Teach the pad finder that boats, decks, and pad-like objects are not the pad
rules.condition: The pad-finder dataset lacks boats without pads, decoy pads, pad-like markings, shadows, deck equipment, people, or other objects near the pad.
rules.label_instruction: Label true pad centers positively. Label boats without pads and other objects as negatives. Do not teach the network that every boat or every bright rectangle is a pad.
rules.rationale: The pad finder must discriminate the actual landing pattern from visually similar structures on the boat and in the background.

rules.title: Separate pad presence from an inferable pad center
rules.condition: The pad is visibly present but its center or geometry is occluded by equipment, water spray, people, or the frame edge.
rules.label_instruction: Presence may remain true if the pad is visibly present, but mask the center and offset when the center is not inferable. Do not invent a center from the visible edge.
rules.rationale: Presence and localization are different targets. A partially visible pad can prove existence without supporting a precise center.

rules.title: Cover pad-finder range, bearing, tilt, lighting, and sea-state bins
rules.condition: Pad-finder data is concentrated at one distance, bearing, camera tilt, lighting condition, or approach direction.
rules.label_instruction: Sample the full acquisition envelope, including pad near image borders, different deck angles, and realistic glare and spray. Reject bins whose labels are not resolvable.
rules.rationale: The pad finder must acquire the pad from whatever approach the search handoff produces, not only from a centered ideal view.

rules.title: Generate labels from the exact rendered camera and timestamp
rules.condition: Labels are not derived from the same frame's camera intrinsics, extrinsics, drone pose, gimbal pose, boat pose, and capture or delivery timestamp.
rules.label_instruction: Recompute labels from the exact frame. Do not reuse labels after camera motion, boat motion, image delay, or a changed gimbal command.
rules.rationale: Heatmap cells and offsets are only valid for the image they were projected into. A stale pose creates systematically shifted labels.

rules.title: Define target identity by a visible signature, not hidden simulator identity
rules.condition: Target identity is defined by a hidden ID, map, scene seed, or a visual feature that is not guaranteed visible at the range where identity is required.
rules.label_instruction: Give the target a persistent visible signature, and generate matched decoys that share hull, color, lighting, and context except for that signature. If the signature is not visible, apply R002 and R007.
rules.rationale: The model can only learn what the camera can see. Hidden identity training is label leakage and produces brittle confidence.

rules.title: Split by map, boat instance, and scenario seed
rules.condition: Train, validation, or test share a map, boat instance, scenario seed, or near-duplicate frames.
rules.label_instruction: Split by map and boat instance before frame sampling. Hold out maps and boats entirely. Do not tune thresholds on the test split.
rules.rationale: Random frame splits leak the same scene into train and test and make synthetic results look better than deployment.

rules.title: Use radio first when usable, and fall back to search on failure
rules.condition: Usable radio is available but the search head is still run, or radio is absent, invalid, contradicted, or points to an empty location and the search head is not activated.
rules.label_instruction: No image labels. Evaluate behavior: usable radio skips search and approaches the radio point, but still requires visual pad confirmation. Invalid, stale, contradicted, or empty-arrival radio activates search and marks radio untrusted.
rules.rationale: Radio can remove the need for a search phase, but it cannot authorize landing by itself. Vision remains the authority for the boat and pad.

rules.title: Gate radio on validity, consistency, and persistence
rules.condition: Radio is used without checking freshness, plausibility, visual agreement, or persistence; or a single bad packet triggers a mode switch.
rules.label_instruction: Use radio only if valid, fresh, plausible, consistent with visual or own-state evidence, and not contradicted. Require a sustained failure before switching to search, and a sustained recovery before switching back.
rules.rationale: A valid-looking packet can still be stale or wrong. Immediate switching causes flapping; blind trust causes landing on a ghost.

rules.title: Do not supervise permission to land from a single frame
rules.condition: A single-frame label is used to supervise target confirmation, permission to approach, handoff, or permission to land.
rules.label_instruction: Perception labels are per-frame. Confirmation and landing permission are state-machine decisions from track stability, evidence, identity, and R15 metric confirmation. Label them on sequences, not stills.
rules.rationale: A frame can look like the target while the track is unstable, the boat is a decoy, or R15 has not confirmed the pad. A still-image permission label teaches shortcuts.

rules.title: Evaluate detection, identity, tracking, handoff, and landing separately
rules.condition: Acceptance uses only aggregate loss or only final landing rate, without stage-wise metrics and radio-mode breakdowns.
rules.label_instruction: Report recall and false positives by range and visibility; evidence and identity accuracy; track stability; confirmation rate; handoff rate; and landing rate. Validate on held-out real or benchmark episodes separately for good, bad, absent, and lying radio.
rules.rationale: A landing failure can come from perception, tracking, handoff, or R15. One aggregate number cannot tell which stage to fix.

rules.title: Balance easy negatives, hard negatives, and edge cases
rules.condition: The dataset is dominated by easy empty sea or large centered boats, or hard negatives and edge cases are too rare to learn.
rules.label_instruction: Set coverage targets by range, visibility, occlusion, boat count, target identity resolvability, and pad visibility. Include hard cases with correct labels or masks, not as label noise.
rules.rationale: A model trained mostly on easy frames looks good in aggregate and fails exactly when search or landing is difficult.
